## Design

### 2026-10-06 – So today i mainly just decided the specifics of what i am going to make

**2.5h**

So today i mainly just decided the specifics of what i am going to make
This is actually an ongoing project that i have had for almost a year where I'm trying to make a keyboard for my friend, so a lot of the decisions are easy.
For example, I know I want it to use some addressable LEDS (probably 5050s) to make cool patterns like rippling when you press a key.
I also know that I want it to be a TKL keyboard, and I know the kind of switches I want to use (cherry MX something (2a?). the one with the clear and light red I don't remember the exact name its this one)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/364a4d1b7e0b95d7b2eb0468e0876f4e82bac87b523fd414677a8f3321902542.png)
I have done some previous work on this project previously but I'm not exactly happy with it and it fell apart the moment I tried to actually design it in kicad (likely because I was (am) bad at kicad), so I'm doing it again.
Specifically, I made some mappings for the rows/columns
![keyboardLayout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/1b95634d8b1cfde8203c25961df9cc33d357a8821df9479415604e253acbf5d6.png)
but as you can see it is bad because the picture I used has a weird layout and that made it hard to trace, so I re-did it
![KeyboardLayout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/5737485c6fa29553e5ad3cb3bd659fecb5a2cae3d2bdde8fafac5c7b104b3e37.jpg)
I'm a little happier with this one. I still think it will become a problem when I try to trace it, but that's a problem for when I trace it.
I also spent a little time (I was at school so couldn't use my actual computer except through ssh :() researching micro controllers because initially I was going to use a Arduino micro but then I though about it for like 30 seconds and there is no way that it will run 50ish addressable LEDs, some kind of graphics thing, and scan an entire keyboard in a reasonable time, so I looked into other options like a pi pico or a teensy or maybe even like an  STM32. if you couldn't tell, I haven't decided on that yet, but that is something I will have in the back of my mind going forward.
so basically I thought a bunch.
I'm not sure if I can work tomorrow, but If I can I will start on the 87 switch schematic grind.

ALSO, while I was writing this the meta key on my keyboard died, thank god for keyd, but I couldn't have picked a better time to work on this

am I supposed to make these cooler than just a text wall?

### 2026-10-08 – I made so much progress today its amazing what you can do with academic negligence and sleep deprivation.

**5h**

I made so much progress today its amazing what you can do with academic negligence and sleep deprivation.
I decided on a microcontroller, arranged all the keys, and started getting the traces wired. lots and lots of boring repetitive work. i only had to re-do something for every key because i made a silly mistake twice though! I'm gonna use a pi pico. upon thinking about it for like 3 seconds i realized its the obvious choice. Its SMD, has plenty of pins, and i can run the input handling and LEDs on separate cores. Speaking of LEDS, I decided on a layout and a type. Im gonna use 5050's

![SMD LED 5050 RGB 0](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/8901f4b3269538fb3a4e572725abccd7f36281df5096d4af7f0a6dabc24fffa2.jpg)

in between every row with about  a key worth of spacing. this only leaves like 0.2mm of clearance on either side, so thats gonna be fun to hand solder, but it just fits way to well.

Here is the layout so far:

![KeyboardPCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/f077e6f89506e6309b0d34948e00dbf6051503337bce8d48f357dbb5c3538085.png)

### 2026-10-09 – made less progress than i hoped :(, but i now know exactly what im going to do!

**4h**

made less progress than i hoped :(, but i now know exactly what im going to do!
the first thing i did was finalize my design for the keyboard. it is going to have a 3d printed shell and a laser cut 1.5mm sanded acrylic key plate (courtesy of my school) screwed on. the PCB will be floating and suspended by the solder joints to the keypad. here is a drawing:

![KeyboardSideView](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/8132a3e71c3e8412c911fe77fb3899aff4be10d71f1b028463aeb65808856e4e.png)

i also decided on how many leds i want and where. there are 90 total leds, which is kinda unfortunate because it means i can only run them at 10% brightness (they draw a LOT of power, like 0.06 amps per pop. all 90 draw like 5 amps max and a usb plug can only supply like 0.9 its crazy) but honestly i shouldent need anything brighter than that. here are all of them in the schematic

![KeyboardSchematic3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/e2605c104f1e15fedbfb94f71b64e8cbaf7b0d627b6ee82906607f366db632b9.png)

there is probably a better way to do that. also, you might notice the capacitors. those are the decoupling capacitors and they are a PAIN THE ASS. every single led needs one, and the require you to make like the shortest possible path between to vcc and ground pins to work optimally, which is unfortunately something i dident design around. and remember how i was complaining about having to route like 87 diodes? yeah i have to route 90 of these and they have like 2 vias and 6 traces a pop. thats a tomorrow adventure.

![DecouplingCapacitor](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/1f6ba07b790eb86f216c971f71729e5eb0ff626f4d91e9331811b82842e67590.png)

anyway, here is the layout thus far:

![KeyboardLayout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/eed6c841d55ffb3a2220662bb9d97686e9210b9c8c39fb2c8fecf8ac0f014593.png)

really looking forward to hand soldering all 90 5mm leds + 87 2mm resistors + 90 1mm capacitors with like 0.2mm of clearance!

.

worst part is  im not even sure if thats sarcasm.

### 2026-10-10 – D E C O U P L I N G     D I O D E S

**2h**

D E C O U P L I N G     D I O D E S
i had to wire up 90 diodes that are connected to like 2 vias a piece and have just enough  repetition to be boring but just enough variation to be annoying. i think this is the most egregious one i squeezed in.

![DecouplingCapacitor2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/dec85185055f08e962165f774276f0ae21791c337f1598e1dd528cd6bbe8ebcd.png)

I also connected all of the rows and columns to their distance brothers (before i only had adjacent switches connected). here is the pcb thus far

![KeyboardLayout2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/9ebcdf0ed9ee7faec3947ef2d733c5f3f9968f5967d70cc746edaa6ec447beef.png)

i was actually kinda hoping to finish today, but then i took like 1 look at the area around the pico, realized i needed to fit 20 traces in there somehow, and decided that thats future ians problem. the end is in sight though. all i need to do is route these final few traces, do a ground pour, and make the silkscreen look pretty, and then the PCB is done!

### 2026-10-10 – The PCB is mechanically done!

**3.5h**

The PCB is mechanically done!
routing the final few traces was kinda crazy and forced me to get a little creative, but honestly was not that bad, aside from almost forgetting the resistor at the start of the LED line. then i had to battle with the DRC because the footprints i used (the 0603 capacitors) had pads that were to close together, so i had to poke around in setting till it stopped yelling at me. it annoys me slightly that everything is not under 0.2mm clearance, but it is not really in my control (unless i want to go through decoupling capacitor hell again) and it probably wont have a impact on cost or performance. i also deleted all the silkscreens because they were overlapping with each other and it looked bad, and that required me to edit the raw file and control F all the layers, which was a little scary, but it worked! and that is basically the last thing i have to do. add the silkscreen and make it look pretty (and then cad and machine the case and plate but thats a battle for another day). Im so close!
